references.text: Phinehas also stopped a plague by intervening with a decisive action, just as Aaron stood between the dead and the living to stop the plague.
This is the parallel verse in the Hebrew numbering (17:13 in some translations), which describes exactly the same event where Aaron stood between the dead and the living.
The atonement money was to be given to avert a plague over the people of Israel, showing the connection between atonement and protection from God's judgment.
David built an altar and offered sacrifices to stop a plague, just as Aaron's incense offering stopped the plague in the wilderness.
David sacrificed on the threshing floor to stop the plague, a parallel example of intercessory action to halt God's judgment.
The psalm refers to Phinehas who stood up and executed judgment, so the plague stopped—a poetic reminder of the role of priestly mediators in stopping God's wrath.
The Lord's suffering servant stood between transgressors and bore the sin of many, a prophetic parallel to Aaron who stood between the dead and the living.
Jesus always lives to intercede for his people, the ultimate mediator that Aaron's action pointed toward.
Christ as mediator between God and humanity, the one who can stop spiritual death and give life.
